description: WAGRI is a public cloud platform in Japan that gathers agricultural data and programs and offers them through APIs, so that ICT vendors and farm machinery makers can build web services and apps for farmers. Its API categories cover weather, farmland, crop growth and yield prediction, market prices, pesticides and fertilisers, pest and disease diagnosis, farm machinery, farm management and maps. It was developed under the Cabinet Office's Cross-ministerial Strategic Innovation Promotion Program (SIP) by a consortium led by the Keio University SFC Research Institute and is operated by the National Agriculture and Food Research Organization (NARO). Coverage is Japan. Access is by membership: data-using members pay 40,000 yen a month per client, with a 20 GB monthly transfer cap and 2,000 yen per extra gigabyte, fees cut in April 2022; data-providing members and a one-year trial plan limited to 100 calls and 25 MB a month are free, with discounts for academia and farm businesses. Caveats: the site is in Japanese, data are for members under WAGRI's terms, and the pages read do not list each API's source or licence. For simulation it provides farmland, weather and growth prediction services that farm digital twins and planning tools can call. It is related to the Climate FieldView record in this catalogue, a commercial farm data platform.
